requirements.requirement: Configure node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance every day at 02:15.
requirements.summary: The root crontab contains the exact 02:15 daily entry, and the OpenRC crond service was enabled and running. After a verified reboot, the entry, executable script, runlevel enablement, and running daemon were all observed again.

The cron entry appends both stdout and stderr to the specified log. Direct executions successfully appended output, the existing log survived reboot, and its line count increased from one to two during the post-restart test.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovery of crond, the schedule, executable script, retained log data, and successful output appending.
limitations: No naturally timed 02:15 cron firing was captured; scheduling is established by the exact crontab entry and active daemon, while output handling was verified through direct executions.
The generic lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because the Alpine node uses OpenRC, although direct OpenRC checks showed crond running before and after restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: The script repair was a necessary prerequisite because the prepared file was non-executable and malformed; cron, log, and service changes implemented the contract; manual executions were bounded evidence; and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The only unnecessary residue was /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log, created by the reboot command and still present afterward. It was not reverted, but it was a bounded, low-risk temporary file. No executor-caused package damage, failed service, or unsafe listener was observed.
